trust_decision.summary: When a redirect is followed automatically, the client decides whether the caller's credentials (Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization) may go to the redirect target. The H3 client never made that decision; the HTTP/1.1/HTTP/2 path decides on host equality alone.

landing_point.why: The summary names the HTTP/3 redirect handler. handle_redirect/11 is the only H3 code that follows a redirect, and at :178 it passes the original Headers unchanged.

fix_sites.entry_point: hackney_h3:request/5 with Opts follow_redirect => true (public low-level H3 API)
fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP/3 client module (second, map-options client next to hackney:request)

fix_sites.entry_point: new helpers maybe_strip_redirect_headers/4, same_origin/2, drop_credential_headers/1, called only from the site above
fix_sites.module_kind: same module, private helpers (exported only under TEST)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches only src/hackney_h3.erl, which is also the landing point.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and NEWS name the HTTP/3 handler only, and NEWS cites 'the HTTP/1.1 path' as the reference behaviour that already strips credentials (CVE-2018-1000007). A solver would treat hackney.erl's host-only check as correct and already fixed.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects must keep credentials, location_trusted => true must keep them across origins, non-credential headers (User-Agent) must survive, and on 307/308 the body is still forwarded. A fix that strips on every redirect, or drops all headers, breaks the fix's own tests and the H1 'same host keeps auth' test.

O6_input_shapes: header name as binary, string (list) or atom (fix.diff:165-167)
header name in any case, compared lower-cased (fix.diff:162)
three credential headers: authorization, cookie, proxy-authorization (fix.diff:159)
origin change by host, by port or by scheme (fix.diff:150-156; port test fix.diff:208-216)
absolute, absolute-path and relative Location resolved before comparison (src/hackney_h3.erl:198-237)

O7_producer.where: Credentials come straight from the caller's Headers argument (src/hackney_h3.erl:121-124). No producer is involved.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: hackney:request with follow_redirect (sync HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, and H3 through hackney_conn) keeps the basic_auth and cookie options on a redirect to the same host but a different scheme or port, e.g. https->http downgrade or :443->:8443. The origin check compares host only.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Advisory scoped to HTTP/3; NEWS calls the HTTP/1.1 path the already-correct reference; existing test only checks host change (test/hackney_redirect_tests.erl:258-287); the CVE-2018-1000007 comment says 'different host'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another file in the same package (src/hackney.erl vs src/hackney_h3.erl), reached through a different public API (hackney:request/5 proplist options vs hackney_h3:request/5 map)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: basic_auth taken from userinfo in the original URL is put into Options (src/hackney.erl:503-506). It survives a same-host, different-port or different-scheme redirect, and add_default_headers sends it over plain HTTP by default because insecure_basic_auth defaults to true.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Looks like a separate insecure_basic_auth policy issue rather than redirect origin handling.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the first route; the userinfo-to-basic_auth step is about 500 lines away from follow_redirect

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The async follow_redirect path currently only sends a {redirect, Location, Headers} message to the owner. A planted auto-follow inside hackney_conn that re-sends the stored request headers without an origin check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Comments at src/hackney_conn.erl:848 and :895 say 'redirect not yet implemented for H3'. A maintainer filling that gap would copy the H3 handler's pre-fix shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Forward the caller's original Headers (not []) on redirect, so a user-supplied Authorization header also crosses the same-host check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Passing [] silently drops custom headers such as Accept on redirect, and a feature request to preserve them is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Origin comparison done on the raw Location prefix rather than the parsed URL (a parser differential, e.g. upper-case scheme or protocol-relative //host, which the resolver currently treats as relative).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: resolve_redirect_url already dispatches on literal prefixes, so a string-prefix origin check would match the surrounding style.

O9_family: credential leak on cross-origin redirect (CWE-601 as filed; closer to CWE-200 / CWE-522)

src/hackney.erl:1039 compares hosts case-sensitively, which fails closed (strips) for case-only differences.
